guide.headline: Osborne's arm and UConn's deep shots carried this one
guide.hook: A freshman quarterback with a 56 percent usage rate threw deep on a defense built to allow it, and Syracuse's own passing-downs edge kept the game from ever getting easy.

items.title: Osborne already threw for 314
items.what: Kalieb Osborne came in completing 81 of 140 for 1164 yards and 10 touchdowns on the year, and in this game alone he went 19 of 39 for 314 yards and three touchdowns with zero interceptions. He also picked up 23 yards on nine carries. For a true freshman carrying 56 percent of UConn's offensive usage, that is a starter's workload and a starter's answer.
items.when: Every dropback, especially third down where he operates 71 percent of passing-down snaps.

items.title: UConn's deep ball hunted Syracuse's safeties
items.what: UConn ranks No. 6 of 138 nationally in pass explosiveness at 1.91, and Syracuse ranks just No. 67 at limiting those explosive passes at 1.54, a 44 percentile point gap. Watch the first deep shot UConn takes and see if Syracuse rolls a second safety over after it lands. If they don't adjust, Osborne's 314 yards and three scores make total sense.
items.when: First deep shot of the game, then every look after it.

items.title: Syracuse kept answering on third-and-long
items.what: Syracuse ranks No. 49 of 138 on passing downs at 35 percent success against a UConn defense that sits at No. 105 at 32 percent, a 41 percentile point gap. That means a third-and-8 was never a guaranteed punt for Syracuse. Two conversions like that in a half is enough to wreck a defensive plan, and this matchup was built for exactly that.

guide.cardLine: A true freshman threw for 314 and three scores by attacking a Syracuse secondary ranked No. 67 against explosive passing.
